body: NUnit doesn't escape control characters in the user message by design, so if it's happening it's a bug. Can you provide a repro test case?
BTW, as a part of the repro, please indicate where the erroneous output appears. We've already had a separate report of this but were never able to find out that information.

No need to repro, I see the problem. Somebody fixed issue #41 "Check for zeroes in assert messages" by leveraging a method designed for a different purpose, which escapes **all** control characters. Specifically, the intent of that method was to be used for the display of expected versus actual values, in which case it's necessary to see all control characters in order to make a visual comparison.

Clearly, we have to escape nulls, even in the user-provided message, in order to avoid errors in the display. Any thoughts on what else - if anything - we should escape?  The method currently being used is here: https://github.com/nunit/nunit/blob/master/src/NUnitFramework/framework/Constraints/MsgUtils.cs#L314
OK, we'll figure out something. I suggest you review the PR when it's available.
Hey guys, let me know if you think PR #1659 looks suitable.
Would it be possible to push this fix as a 3.4.2 hotfix on nuget?

@13xforever we will not release this as a hotfix, but if you need this fix, you can use our CI NuGet feed until the next release. To do so, add a NuGet.config file to the root of your solution and add our CI NuGet feed to it as an [additional package source](https://docs.nuget.org/consume/nuget-config-file#package-sources). The address for our feed is, https://ci.appveyor.com/nuget/nunit

Once you do that, if you select pre-release in the package explorer, you can upgrade NUnit to version 3.5.0-CI-3020-master which contains this fix.

issue.title: String unescaping bug and a few questions

repository.name: docs
repository.description: Documentation for all active NUnit projects

issue.body:
Hello. I am investigating the [issue of why](https://github.com/fsprojects/FsUnit/issues/96#issuecomment-243082543) the message string passed into assert unescapes the newline characters and I thought to ask here first. I am also looking at the source, but it is not really obvious to me just by the brief scan that I did. I have some questions as well.

1) If a class has an IDisposable interface implemented, will that automatically get called after the test is over or is an explicit TearDown attribute necessary? I did not see that noted in the manual, so it might be worth adding.

2) If the tests are run in parallel, will each thread create its own instance of the class being tested or will that class be shared? Knowing that might be important. I had not seen that noted in the manual as well.

3) In the [Platform Attribute page](https://github.com/nunit/docs/wiki/Platform-Attribute) there is a slight omission. Specifically:

```
If a test or fixture with the Platform attribute does not satisfy the specified platform requirements it is skipped. The test does not affect the outcome of the run at all: it is not considered as ignored and is not even counted in the total number of tests. [Ed.: Check this.] In the gui, the tree node for the test remains gray and the status bar color is not affected.
```

Note the `Ed.: Check this.` that was made all the way back in January. I am guessing the author completely forgot about it by now.

issue.body:
Program:

```
open FsUnitTyped
open NUnit.Framework

1 |> shouldEqual 2
1 |> shouldNotEqual 2
```

Output:

```
NUnit.Framework.AssertionException:   Expected: 2\nActual: 1
  Expected: True
  But was:  False
```

What bothers me is that `\n` that is printed as a part of the actual string. This is my first time using both FsUnit and NUnit, but that can't be right.

issue.title: ANSI characters in Console Output
issue.body:
I'm trying to push ANSI color characters through the test output and into the console for highlighting key-items in my test output. I'm able to do this successfully outside of NUnit (writing directly to `Console.Out`), but it looks like the colors are being overwritten by the appender. I was wondering if you guys had any insight as to why this might not be working? I've been digging through the code, but haven't identified anything yet.
- Worth noting, the ansi codes I am pushing are being intercepted (not printed to console).

Before you try to stop me:
- I know ANSI has limited terminal support, but we are running in bash and displaying final results in custom reporting tool that is capable of parsing these characters.
- We are using NUnit for integration tests (using Selenium) which have lengthy output describing each step taken, so separating output into smaller unit-tests is not an option.
